# New-ZbxMaintenance

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a maintenance period.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxMaintenance [[-Name] <string>] [-MaintenanceType <ZabbixMaintenanceDataCollectionType>] [-Description <string>] [-ActiveSince <DateTimeOffset>] [-ActiveTill <DateTimeOffset>] [-TagsEvalType <ZabbixEvalType>] [-Tag <ZabbixMaintenanceTagRequest[]>] [-Group <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHostGroup>[]>] [-HostReference <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHost>[]>] [-TimePeriod <ZabbixMaintenanceTimePeriodRequest[]>] [-Trigger <ZabbixReference<ZabbixTrigger>[]>] [-EventName <ZabbixMaintenanceEventNameRequest[]>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A maintenance period suppresses problems, and optionally data collection, for hosts and host groups during planned work. The New-ZbxMaintenance cmdlet sends maintenance.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new maintenance period back with maintenance.get and writes it. The server requires -Name, -ActiveSince, -ActiveTill and -TimePeriod; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Put a host into maintenance for the next two hours

```powershell
$now = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$window = New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod -TimePeriodType Onetime -StartDate $now -Period 7200
New-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch window' -Host 'web-01' -ActiveSince $now -ActiveTill ($now + 7200) -TimePeriod $window |
    Select-Object MaintenanceId, Name, MaintenanceType, ActiveSince, ActiveTill
```

-ActiveSince/-ActiveTill bound the maintenance (Unix seconds); the one-time period inside it is built with New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod. -HostReference (alias -Host) takes host names, ids or objects. Data is still collected (Normal).

### Example 2: Stop data collection for a group during a planned outage

```powershell
$start = [DateTimeOffset]::new([datetime]::UtcNow.Date.AddDays(1).AddHours(22)).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$window = New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod -TimePeriodType Onetime -StartDate $start -Period (4 * 3600)
New-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Database upgrade' -Group 'Linux servers' -MaintenanceType Nodata -Description 'PostgreSQL 16 upgrade' -ActiveSince $start -ActiveTill ($start + 4 * 3600) -TimePeriod $window |
    Select-Object Name, MaintenanceType, Description
```

-MaintenanceType Nodata tells the server to drop incoming data for the hosts while the window is on. -Group takes host group names, ids or objects; -Description is free text shown in the frontend.

### Example 3: Suppress only the problems that carry a tag

```powershell
$now = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$window = New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod -TimePeriodType Onetime -StartDate $now -Period 3600
$null = New-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Checkout release' -Host 'web-01', 'db-01' -Tag @{ tag = 'env'; operator = 0; value = 'prod' } -ActiveSince $now -ActiveTill ($now + 3600) -TimePeriod $window
(Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Checkout release' -SelectTags -SelectHosts) | Select-Object Name, @{ n = 'Hosts'; e = { $_.Hosts.TechnicalName -join ', ' } }, @{ n = 'Tags'; e = { $_.Tags | ForEach-Object { '{0}={1}' -f $_.tag, $_.value } } }
```

With data collection on, -Tag limits the maintenance to problems whose tags match; other problems on the same hosts still alert. Each tag is a hashtable (operator 2 = Like, 0 = Equals).
